1) we propose a novel method for consolidating image feature representations from multiple task-specific teachers, 2) this method improves downstream performance on novel recognition tasks over the teacher(s) and a strong baseline, and 3) we provide a theoretical analysis of why our method is effective.

we present an efficient method to learn a single image feature representation from task-specific teacher representations that outperforms the teacher (or the best of all teachers).
our work is the first to show that task-specific teacher(s) can be consolidated into a generalist model, which is a more practical and scalable approach to multi-task learning.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a simple and effective approach to consolidate knowledge from multiple expert teachers into a single generalist student.
a multi-task distillation framework can be used to transfer knowledge from multiple task-specific teachers to a consolidated image representation.
we show that a simple distillation strategy can improve transferability from task-specific teachers to novel tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the representation of a task-specific teacher is not necessarily a good feature representation for a downstream task, and that consolidation is needed to improve downstream transfer performance.
the representation learned from a single teacher is not always the optimal one, and that a consolidated representation can be learned with a few extra unlabeled data.
the representation learned from multiple task-specific teachers can be consolidated to a more transferable representation, which can be used to improve the performance of a downstream task.
